A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same puppeteering-defense study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. The appendices match apart from page numbers; v3 additionally includes a checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments across three datasets and five generators, cross-domain evaluations, ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same two-head EBL representation, pose-conditioned contrastive objective, frozen generator encoder, extreme-pose filtering, and LSTM temporal aggregation. The architecture and training description in Appendix D are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate NVIDIA-VC, RAVDESS, and CREMA-D with 3DFaceShop, MCNet, EmoPortraits, SDFR, and LivePortrait. Authorized versus puppeteered videos, cross-domain evaluation, pose variation, and appearance modifications cover the same scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Vahdati et al. and the same seven deepfake detectors. Avatar Fingerprinting remains excluded. Corrected TALL and CLRNet citations identify existing comparators rather than introduce new evaluated methods.

E3.justification: The identity-disjoint splits, Table 3 sample counts, pooled versus NVIDIA-VC-only training, AUC/RER metrics, and experimental configurations remain unchanged. The checklist's newly stated training cost does not establish a changed training budget.

E4.justification: Both retain component ablations in Tables 4 and 7, yaw sensitivity in Table 5, appearance robustness in Table 6, and temporal-window and training-identity analyses in Figure 4. The supplementary analyses were already present in v1.

E5.justification: No run counts, concrete seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added. The new checklist asserts statistical significance with an empty justification and refers to a random seed without supplying one.

E6.justification: Section 5.2.1 corrects the attribution of CLRNet's 0.684 AUC from SDFR on NVIDIA-VC to MCNet on CREMA-D, matching Table 1 in both PDFs. Numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and plotted results remain unchanged; this is a reporting correction, not a performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes its generator arguments from g(z_t^k, R^ell) to g(z_t^ell, R^k), revising the formal assignment of driving and target identities. The unchanged output superscript and following sentence leave a residual inconsistency. Proposition 1, the loss mathematics, and the Appendix G proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about latent-only, enrollment-free biometric-leakage detection, real-time operation, and generalization. Changing the title from 'Disarm' to 'Expose' does not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of pose dominance, identity diversity, temporal fusion, and appearance robustness remain unchanged. The same limitations concerning pose, occlusion, lighting, and motion blur remain, alongside the same demographic and applicability qualifications in Appendices E–F.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository pointer claiming code and trained-model availability. Its checklist newly reports approximately 18 GPU-hours on an RTX 3090 and describes licensing and output-watermarking plans; Appendix D's implementation details are unchanged. The checklist's future-release wording conflicts with the abstract's availability statement, and actual repository availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Background works in references 1–3 and 52 are replaced, and a dedicated CLRNet reference 72 is added. Other extensive bibliographic edits largely update metadata for recognizable existing works. The related-work narrative and positioning against prior puppeteering defenses remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title wording, author ordering and affiliation presentation, and conference header; it adds acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist and revises bibliographic details. The scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 are enlarged, Figure 1's caption moves below the illustration, and Tables 3–4 are reformatted with different wrapping and placement. Other material reflows across pages. No scientific figures or tables are added or removed, and the appendix displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves traceability and usability through corrected baseline citations, the Table 1 result-attribution correction, code/model access information, and larger displays. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems introduced by the checklist, including its denial of formal theory despite Proposition 1 and its unsupported statistical-significance assertion. The revision improves presentation and documentation without resolving all internal inconsistencies.
